title: 2013 HMMT November General Problem 4
statement: A 50 -card deck consists of 4 cards labeled " \(i\) " for \(i=1,2, \ldots, 12\) and 2 cards labeled " 13 ". If Bob randomly chooses 2 cards from the deck without replacement, what is the probability that his 2 cards have the same label?

solutions.text: \(\frac{73}{1225}\) All pairs of distinct cards (where we distinguish cards even with the same label) are equally likely. There are \(\binom{2}{2}+12\binom{4}{2}=73\) pairs of cards with the same label and \(\binom{50}{2}=100 \cdot \frac{49}{4}=1225\) pairs of cards overall, so the desired probability is \(\frac{73}{1225}\).
